item.title: Discretisation in algebraic $K$-theory of independent ample groupoids and their Steinberg algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.38791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An independent ample groupoid $G$ comes equipped with a discrete groupoid $G_d$ and a proper \'etale correspondence $\Omega:G_d\to G$. Discretisation with respect to a homological invariant $\mathcal{H}$ holds when $\mathcal{H}(\Omega)$ is an equivalence. We show for example that discretisation with respect to the $K$-theory spectrum $\mathbb{K} \mathfrak{B}_G$ of the permutative category of bisections always holds, establish excision and continuity for this invariant, and use all this and explicit resolutions by independent groupoids to compute it for several families of ample groupoids. We also prove discretisation with respect to invariants of the Steinberg algebra $\ell[G]$ such as (homotopy) algebraic $K$-theory in several particular cases, and carry out computations.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Corti\~nas, Xin Li

item.title: Analytic Kasparov product for non-separable C$^*$-algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.40351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an analytic framework for the explicit construction of Kasparov products on uncountably generated Hilbert modules over non-separable C$^*$-algebras by extending the classical Kasparov bimodule picture. In particular, this yields a well-defined functor from the category of general C$^*$-algebras whose restriction to separable C$^*$-algebras coincides with classical KK-theory and which satisfies several properties expected of non-separable KK-theory. A key idea of the extension is to replace a single Fredholm operator on a Kasparov bimodule with a net and to encode the directed system of separable C$^*$-subalgebras. We also introduce the notion of freely complementable Hilbert modules and develop cropping techniques to extend Kasparov's technical theorem beyond the countably generated setting. It naturally gives rise to a sufficiently broad class of C$^*$-algebras that provides a non-commutative analogue of paracompactness and includes all $\sigma$-unital algebras.
item.dc:creator: Ikhan Choi

item.title: On the cohomological dimension of Henselian valued fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.37961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(K,v)$ be a Henselian valued field of rank one and of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, with value group $\Gamma$ dense in $\mathbb{R}$ and residue field $k$. We compute all the graded pieces of the filtration induced by $v$ on the Milnor $\mathrm{K}$-theory modulo $p$ of $K$, in terms of the exterior powers of the $\mathbb{F}_p$-vector space $\Gamma/p\Gamma$ and of the modules of differential forms of $k$. This extends to the non-discrete setting a classical theorem of Kato concerning complete discretely valued fields. We also prove that, when $(K,v)$ is maximally complete, no class escapes this filtration by accumulating at a limit. As an application, we prove the inequality $\dim_p(K)\geq\dim_{\mathbb{F}_p}(\Gamma/p\Gamma)+\dim_p(k)$ between Kato's $p$-dimensions, and we show that it becomes an equality as soon as $(K,v)$ is maximally complete.
item.dc:creator: Diego Izquierdo, Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche, Gonzalo Manzano Flores

item.title: A short proof of the Segal conjecture for $C_p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.39440v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new proof of the generalized Segal conjecture for the cyclic group of prime order p, i.e. the fact that the Tate diagonal of any bounded below spectrum is a p-completion. The idea, inspired by Hahn and Wilson's argument, is to use descent along the equivariant map from the p-fold tensor power of the field with p elements to its topological Hochschild homology. The only computational input that we use is the calculation of the homotopy rings of this topological Hochschild homology and its Tate construction, together with the map induced by the cyclotomic Frobenius.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Nikolaus

item.title: On equivariant affineness in elliptic cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2610.39583v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate equivariant affineness in spectral algebraic geometry: the phenomenon where $\infty$-categories of quasi-coherent sheaves of a spectral stack are equivalent to $\infty$-categories of modules over an equivariant ring spectrum. In the nonequivariant case, this is known as 0-affineness, and has been studied by Gaitsgory, Mathew--Meier, amongst others. Allowing for equivariant phenomena opens up a much wider class of spectral stacks to be studied through the lens of spectra. The spectral stacks at the heart of our analysis are oriented elliptic curves, their associated Hilbert schemes, and related constructions. When working over the universal base, so the moduli stack of oriented elliptic curves, we show that these spectral stacks are $U(1)$-, $U(n)$-, and $SU(n)$-equivariantly affine, with associated $G$-ring spectrum Gepner--Meier's equivariant topological modular forms $\mathrm{TMF}_G$. Our results also encompass the groups $Sp(n)$ as well as all finite products of such groups. Our most general result is a relative statement over an arbitrary base stack. These results can be viewed as an integral and global refinement of Greenlees' algebraic model for modules over rational $U(1)$-equivariant elliptic cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Jack Morgan Davies, Sil Linskens, Leonard Tokic

item.title: A groupoid approach to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2604.25595v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we develop a groupoid approach to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture. For a bounded geometry metric space $X$ equipped with a proper, free, and isometric action of a countable discrete group $\Gamma$, we introduce the equivariant coarse groupoid $G(X, \Gamma)$. We prove that the groupoid Baum--Connes conjecture for $G(X, \Gamma)$ with coefficients in $\ell^{\infty}(X,\K)^\Ga$ is equivalent to the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture for $(X, \Gamma)$ using a localization algebra description of groupoid equivariant $KK$-theory on the Rips complex models. As applications of this framework, we prove that if the space $X$ admits a coarse embedding into Hilbert space (which is not required to be $\Gamma$-equivariant), then the equivariant coarse Novikov conjecture holds for $(X, \Gamma)$, i.e., the assembly map $\mu_{X,\Ga}$ is an injection. We also obtain a new proof of the equivariant coarse Baum--Connes conjecture if $X$ admits an equivariant coarse embedding into Hilbert space.
item.dc:creator: Liang Guo

item.title: Quantitative $K$-homology of uniform Roe algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.34050v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce quantitative $K$-homology for uniform Roe algebras of discrete proper metric spaces with bounded geometry, based on the controlled $KK$-theory of Willett and Yu. We construct a comparison map from Lipschitz $K$-theory and prove that, for chain geodesic spaces, it is an isomorphism in a quantitative sense; in particular, quantitative $K$-homology is isomorphic to the inverse limit of the Lipschitz $K$-theory groups as the Lipschitz constant tends to zero. We also establish a pairing between quantitative $K$-homology and quantitative $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Hao Guo, Chenxi Wang, Guoliang Yu

item.title: The $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic Gysin map
item.description: arXiv:2604.24888v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a $\mathbf{P}^1$-unstable non-$\mathbf{A}^1$-invariant theory of motivic spaces and spectra, and construct the Gysin map therein for regular immersions. This in particular gives the Gysin map in the Annala--Hoyois--Iwasa $\mathbf{P}^1$-motivic spectra, and thus gives a uniform construction for the Gysin maps of various cohomology theories.
item.dc:creator: Longke Tang
